ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List (1267/1988/1989), OFAC SDN list, EU CFSP/CP931 designations, the Egyptian national terrorist entities list issued under Law 80/2002 and implementing circulars, and Interpol Red Notices. PEP status triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD), source-of-wealth documentation, and senior-management approval; EDD requires beneficial ownership identification at a 10% threshold for PEPs and risk-sensitive structures while the statutory standard threshold remains 25% for low-risk profiles; screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years per EMLCU record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investor Services Center; electronic name clearance through the official GAFI portal (www.gafi.gov.eg) and the unified National Commercial Registry maintained by the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LLC statutory name must be rendered in Arabic script and may carry a Romanized transliteration as a secondary trading name. The name must identify the activity or a distinctive token and must include the phrase 'LLC' (شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة). It must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name or a protected trademark in Egypt, must not mislead the public or counterparties, and must not be contrary to public order.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Presidency, Ministry or any sovereign title
Army, Military, Police, Security or Intelligence
Petroleum, Gas or any energy cartel token
Religious tokens (Islamic, Fatwa, Mosque, Church) without prior ministerial or Dar al-Iftaa approval
Civil aviation tokens (Aviation, Airline, Air Cargo, Sky) without EGCAA pre-clearance
International, Global, Holding or Group without substantive qualified capital structure
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, GAFI issues a written refusal specifying the conflicting name or sensitive token. The applicant may file an administrative grievance with the GAFI Legal and Technical Complaints Committee within 30 calendar days of the refusal, attaching a fresh Arabic name in priority order, a trademark search report from the Egyptian Trademark Office, and a supporting memorandum; the Committee must issue its decision within 30 days. A further appeal lies with the Egyptian State Council (Administrative Court) within 60 days under State Council Law No. 10/1972 (as amended) and Companies Law No. 194/2020. A granted reservation is valid for 90 days and may be extended once for an additional 90 days upon written request and payment before expiry; if unused, the name is re-released to the registry pool.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A virtual or serviced office may serve exclusively as the administrative registered address if a valid lease or ownership certificate is filed with GAFI, but it can never satisfy the operational commercial-substance requirement of the licensed in-flight catering kitchen. The production premises must be a physically identifiable, hygienically approved and aviation-security-compliant kitchen in airport-bonded or airport-adjacent premises acceptable to the Egyptian General Authority for Civil Aviation (EGCAA) and the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA), supported by a substantive lease of at least one year.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; estimated 60-75% probability of at least one unannounced on-site inspection by GAFI, EGCAA and/or NFSA within the first 12 months of licensing, plus mandatory annual hygiene and aviation-security audits carried out after ramp-access commencement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, particularly the limited liability company provisions in Articles 102 et seq., as read with the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association of a Limited Liability Company (LLC), submitted through the GAFI electronic filing system
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A minimum paid-up capital of EGP 50,000 is required for an Egyptian LLC under Law 159/1981; the full amount must be deposited in a temporary bank escrow account or evidenced by a bank certificate before incorporation, and the blocked funds may be released only after the Commercial Registry/GAFI registration certificate is issued
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders having subscribed and fully paid the initial issued capital, the registered office shall be and is hereby fixed at the executive office of the Company, being the premises described in the submitted lease, until changed by a subsequent resolution. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors accepts the subscriptions of the founding shareholders and authorizes the Chairperson/Managing Director to execute the incorporation contract and all applications with GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the tax authority and the social insurance authority. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chairperson/Managing Director and [Name] be appointed Finance Director/Company Secretary, with sole and joint signature authority for banking, tax and administrative transactions, effective upon the date of issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Registration Legal Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop Investor Center (Cairo headquarters and online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GAFI electronic portal or attend the One-Stop Shop; submit three alternative trade names in Arabic and English for the LLC. Ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not contravene public order. Obtain the name reservation certificate, which is valid for 60 days and must match the future incorporation contract.
required_dossiers: Signed name reservation application form
Copy of founding shareholders' valid national ID or passport
Memorandum explaining the chosen trade name and proposed commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects a proposed name, reformat or add distinguishing elements and resubmit; the applicant may also appeal the refusal to the GAFI Legal Affairs Unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Escrow and Deposit Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt, preferably through the bank branch located within the GAFI One-Stop Shop precinct
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate current account in the name of the company to be formed. Deposit not less than the minimum paid-up capital, at least EGP 50,000, and obtain a bank certificate of blocked deposit or payment guarantee in favor of the proposed company. The bank will apply standard anti-money-laundering customer due diligence, including identification of beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Draft incorporation contract and draft articles of association
Copies of founders' national IDs/passports
Beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds documentation
Initial board resolution by the founding shareholders approving the capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide additional audited financial statements or bank references; where the bank declines the account, substitute an unconditional bank guarantee from another CBE-licensed bank or challenge under the bank's internal complaint procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Incorporation Contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Tawthiq) within the GAFI One-Stop Shop or a competent district notary office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the Arabic-language incorporation contract and articles of association are finalized with the registered office, shareholders, capital split, and management appointments. All founders, or their duly notarized attorneys-in-fact, must appear before the notary to acknowledge signatures. Pay the notarial fees and documentary stamp duty; the notary issues a sealed execution certificate that becomes the statutory foundation document for GAFI.
required_dossiers: Final incorporation contract and articles of association in Arabic
Bank capital deposit certificate or bank guarantee
GAFI name reservation certificate
Original and copy of each founder's valid national ID or passport
Notarized power of attorney if a founder signs through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a founder is unavailable, execute a supplementary notarized power of attorney and resubmit; if the notary observes a substantive discrepancy, amend the contract by a notarized addendum rather than rewriting the instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized incorporation file to GAFI for statutory review. Confirm the LLC name, registered office, paid-up capital and director details. GAFI will register the company, issue the Certificate of Incorporation, and, through its integrated portal, coordinate the creation of the Commercial Register number. The original certificate must be kept as the foundational corporate governance document.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract and articles of association
Bank certificate of paid-up capital or bank guarantee
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership certificate)
Signed first board resolution appointing directors and officers
Passport/national ID copies and qualification declarations of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI queries or returns the file, correct the noted deficiencies with a notarized addendum or supplementary declaration and resubmit; if GAFI remains silent after the statutory period, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Investment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry, Tax, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the GAFI certificate, complete the commercial registration form to obtain the final Commercial Register extract. Immediately thereafter open a corporate tax file with ETA for income tax, VAT registration if applicable, and payroll withholding registration. Register the LLC with NOSI and obtain the social insurance file number for current or planned employees. For the catering activity, the tax card must state the precise ISIC 5621 activity.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate of Incorporation
Notarized incorporation contract and articles of association
Commercial Register extract application form
Certificate of lease of registered office
Tax card application and VAT registration forms (if required)
Social insurance registration forms and employer data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA demands a physical inspection, request a same-day inspection through the GAFI One-Stop Shop; if any fine or late registration penalty is asserted, pay under protest and appeal to the competent tax tribunal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication and Activation of Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Department and the corporate bank branch holding the escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange for publication of the incorporation abstract in an Arabic-language daily newspaper as required under the Companies Law. Present the Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Register extract to the escrow bank to authorize release of the blocked capital into the operational corporate account. Execute the corporate banking cards, issue share certificates to the shareholders, and open the statutory registers and corporate seal.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Register extract
Tax card
Board resolution approving release of escrow and opening of operational bank account
Valid IDs of authorized signatories and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the escrow bank rejects the release, provide written confirmation from GAFI of the company's existence and an updated board resolution; if the publication is delayed, request an extension from GAFI before the expiry of the prescribed publication window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) and National Food Safety Authority (NFSA), coordinated through the GAFI One-Stop Shop licensing window
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment License for Airline In-Flight Catering Operations and, where applicable, Industrial Operating License for Food Manufacturing under Law 15 of 2017

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Environmental Impact Assessment scoping and environmental compliance report required for food processing/catering facilities with moderate atmospheric and liquid discharges; a full EIA report is not required unless the facility exceeds ministerial capacity thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to public sewer must comply with Law 93 of 1962 and its executive regulations, including standards for pH, BOD, COD, TSS and fats-oils-grease; point-source atmospheric emissions and fugitive odors must meet Law 4 of 1994 as amended; hazardous waste, expired products and cooking-oil residues must be segregated and handled through EEAA-licensed waste contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate under Law 12 of 1985 after inspection of fire suppression systems, kitchen hood extinguishing equipment, means of egress and stairwell pressurization; structural load inspection certificate for kitchen equipment and delivery staging areas; Ministry of Labour occupational health and workplace clearance under Labor Law 12 of 2003, including medical fitness certificates for food handlers and high-risk catering personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), under the Ministry of Finance. Taxpayer registration, tax-file administration, VAT registration, electronic invoicing, electronic receipts, declarations, and payment services are administered through the ETA electronic tax portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg and related electronic platforms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Egyptian LLC must obtain a unified tax registration number and open an income-tax file with the competent ETA office based on its registered address. The standard process is: (1) complete incorporation and obtain the Commercial Register and required business-license documentation; (2) obtain the company tax card or electronic tax-registration certificate from the ETA; (3) submit the constitutional documents, Commercial Register, company address evidence, articles of association, identification of managers or authorized representatives, and power of attorney where applicable; (4) obtain VAT registration when the statutory threshold is exceeded or voluntary registration is accepted; (5) complete ETA portal enrollment, authorized-user verification, digital certificate and electronic-signature procedures where required; and (6) obtain an electronic-invoicing profile and integrate approved ERP, API, or portal issuance channels. A non-resident foreign entity with an Egyptian taxable activity, permanent establishment, Egyptian-source income, or VAT obligations must register with the ETA through its Egyptian tax representative or authorized representative and provide certified constitutional, tax-residence, authority, and business documents, with Arabic translation and legalization or apostille where required. Non-resident registration does not by itself create an Egyptian legal entity; an Egyptian branch, subsidiary, permanent establishment, or other taxable presence may require separate commercial and regulatory registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election for an Egyptian LLC. An Egyptian LLC is ordinarily taxed as a separate legal person for corporate income tax and VAT purposes. No general statutory hybrid-mismatch election changes the LLC's default classification. Separate applications or eligibility conditions may apply for investment-law incentives, free-zone treatment, special economic-zone treatment, tax treaty relief, or approved tax-accounting arrangements; these are incentive or relief regimes and not entity-classification elections. A branch or permanent establishment of a foreign company is generally taxed under the rules applicable to a non-resident enterprise and is not interchangeable with an Egyptian LLC merely by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Egypt's Value Added Tax Law No. 67 of 2016 and its executive regulations, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover, subject to the statutory turnover calculation and applicable regulatory rules. Registration may also be required without relying on the threshold for specified activities, imports, taxable supplies subject to special rules, or other statutory cases. Importers and non-residents may have registration or collection obligations independently of the domestic turnover threshold. Voluntary registration may be available subject to ETA conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates a mandatory electronic-invoicing regime for in-scope business-to-business transactions and other categories brought into scope by ETA decisions and implementation phases. Taxpayers must register on the ETA electronic-invoicing platform, obtain or use an approved electronic signature, issue structured electronic invoices containing prescribed supplier, customer, tax, item, value, and unique-identification data, and transmit the invoice through the ETA portal or an approved API or ERP integration. The ETA assigns or validates a unique invoice identifier and may electronically validate or reject submissions. Electronic receipts apply to covered business-to-consumer transactions under the applicable implementation timetable. Paper invoices generally do not satisfy electronic-invoicing obligations once the relevant taxpayer and transaction are in scope. In-flight catering suppliers should assess whether invoices to airlines, airport operators, and other corporate customers fall within mandatory electronic invoicing, and whether ramp delivery, bonded-kitchen, import, customs, or airport-security systems impose additional documentation controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Egypt to a destination outside Egypt may qualify for VAT at 0% if the transaction satisfies the VAT Law, executive regulations, customs requirements, and ETA documentary conditions. The exporter must substantiate the actual export, identify the goods and purchaser, retain the commercial and customs records, and establish that the goods left Egyptian territory. Certain services supplied to non-residents may qualify for zero rating where the statutory conditions are met, including qualifying offshore use or benefit outside Egypt and compliance with documentary and payment evidence requirements. Services performed or consumed in Egypt generally do not become zero-rated merely because the customer is a non-resident or an international airline. Meals prepared and delivered in Egypt to an aircraft at an Egyptian airport should generally be treated as a domestic taxable supply unless a specific customs, bonded, export, or special-zone rule applies and is fully documented. Export VAT refunds or input-tax recovery require valid purchase invoices, customs evidence, VAT filings, proof of payment and export proceeds where requested, and reconciliation of output and input tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Egyptian Customs export declaration or equivalent validated export record
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, quantities, values, currency, VAT treatment, and destination
Packing list and transport document, including bill of lading, airway bill, or other carrier evidence as applicable
Evidence that the goods physically exited Egypt and were accepted by customs at the export point
Certificate of origin where required by the destination, customs authorities, trade arrangement, or customer
VAT invoice or electronic invoice and supporting sales ledger entry
Bank evidence of export proceeds or other approved payment evidence where required by the ETA, banking, customs, or foreign-exchange rules
Contracts, purchase orders, delivery records, airway or ramp-delivery records, and evidence linking the exported goods to the relevant customs declaration
For bonded or airport supplies, applicable bonded-warehouse, customs-control, duty-free, or special-zone authorization and inventory reconciliation records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and Customs Authority may deny zero rating, disallow input VAT recovery, recover incorrectly refunded or unpaid VAT, assess the applicable VAT retrospectively, and impose statutory late-payment interest and administrative penalties. Scrutiny commonly addresses false or incomplete customs declarations, mismatch between invoices and export declarations, failure to prove physical export, fictitious customers or transactions, invalid electronic invoices, unsupported input VAT, related-party pricing, missing bank evidence, and diversion of bonded goods into the domestic market. Fraudulent or deliberately evasive conduct may trigger tax-evasion charges, substantial fines, criminal liability for responsible individuals, suspension or cancellation of tax registration, customs sanctions, seizure or forfeiture, and loss of export or bonded privileges. The 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation period should be treated as a compliance control for export proceeds, subject to applicable Central Bank of Egypt, banking, customs, sectoral, and approved-extension rules; non-compliance may result in banking or export-control consequences and can undermine refund substantiation. The business should maintain a transaction-level export file and reconcile customs, ETA, accounting, airline-contract, inventory, and bank records for the statutory retention period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Foreign Exchange Operations Sector and Banking Control Sector. The CBE is the sole monetary, foreign-exchange and banking control authority under the Unified Banking Law No. 194 of 2020, operating the interbank EGP/USD trading platform, regulating authorised FX dealers, administering import/export trade-payment documentation, monitoring export proceeds repatriation, and licensing all deposit-taking institutions in the Arab Republic of Egypt. No separate foreign-exchange administration exists outside the CBE.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP is convertible on current-account transactions in line with Egypt's IMF Article VIII commitments and the Unified Banking Law No. 194 of 2020. Trade payments for goods and services, royalty payments, and routine overseas expenses may be executed through authorised banks at market-determined interbank rates without item-by-item CBE licence. Capital-account convertibility is partial: inward equity subscription in an Egyptian LLC and registered shareholder loans are protected transfers once declared to the receiving bank; subsequent dividend remittance, loan servicing and capital repatriation may be effected without pre-approval, but each outward transfer is subject to documentary validation. Key profit-remittance hurdles are: (i) the bank must hold audited financial statements, a dividend board resolution, and proof that the 10% withholding tax (or treaty-reduced rate, where applicable) on dividends was filed and paid to the Egyptian Tax Authority; (ii) an ETA tax-clearance certificate is normally demanded for large or recurring outward dividend wires; (iii) in periods of USD liquidity stress, CBE prioritisation can impose queuing of T+2 to T+5 on large outbound transfers; and (iv) EGP is not deliverable offshore, so all foreign-currency liabilities must be covered from foreign-currency balances or converted onshore. Overall, the regime is a managed, trade-liberal system — safe for registered FDI trade flows, but not to be treated as unrestricted capital-account convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The catering LLC must repatriate the full foreign-currency value of export proceeds, including bonded in-flight meal uplifts recognised as customs exports, so that the funds are credited to an account at an authorised Egyptian bank within 90 calendar days of the customs export declaration or airline uplift document date. The obligation is 100% repatriation, not 100% mandatory conversion into EGP: under the post-December-2022 flexible-exchange-rate framework, the CBE has not imposed a forced conversion ratio at receipt, and proceeds may be retained in the invoice currency in a foreign-currency account for onward import settlement, debt service or treasury deployment. To close each export file, the LLC must file with its bank the NAFEZA single-window export declaration, commercial invoice, airway bill or airline uplift manifest, the IATA flight schedule reference, and the CBE export-monitoring registration reference. The bank matches the inbound FX credit to the export documents and releases funds to the treasury account. Non-repatriation within the statutory window can trigger CBE monetary penalties, downgrading of the exporter's banking file, suspension of future import FX allocations, and mandatory AML reporting to the Egyptian Money-Laundering and Terrorist-Financing Combating Unit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW — offshore digital EMIs are not a legally viable primary banking rail in Egypt. The Unified Banking Law No. 194 of 2020 reserves deposit-taking, foreign-currency dealing and payment-account services to CBE-licensed banks and their licensed payment-technology subsidiaries. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business or Currencycloud cannot hold EGP, cannot satisfy the 90-day export-proceeds repatriation rule, and are not recognised for capital injection or dividend remittance clearance. The CBE requires all export receipts to land via SWIFT/RTGS in an Egyptian licensed bank account. An EMI may be used only as an auxiliary collection tool for non-Egypt, non-export ancillary receivables; any such funds must be swept onward to the Egyptian anchor bank and will trigger enhanced due diligence. The recommended architecture is a single Tier-1 Egyptian bank as treasury anchor, supplemented, only if an airline counterparty insists, by a USD concentration account at a recognised foreign branch of a CBE-licensed bank rather than an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or qualified-equivalent compliance interview is effectively mandatory for first-time foreign-owned corporate clients. CBE AML instructions under Law No. 80 of 2002 and its Executive Regulations require face-to-face identification of signatories, directors and ultimate beneficial owners. Tier-1 Egyptian banks generally do not permit fully remote video-only onboarding for a non-resident parent company; at least one compliance meeting at an Egyptian branch is required, although certain banks will accept a meeting at a qualifying overseas branch with apostilled or consularised corporate documents. Budget for one in-person Cairo visit to execute the account-opening mandate and signatory specimens. After onboarding, remote electronic banking is standard. The local Egyptian resident manager may sign under a notarised power of attorney with one physical visit for signature verification. The expected decision cycle is 7 to 14 business days after delivery of the complete KYC pack.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO and multi-layer foreign-parent chain obscuring ultimate ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified and apostilled or consularised commercial registration and constitutional documents for each entity in the ownership chain; passport copies of all directors and the individual UBO; organizational chart with exact shareholding percentages; notarised beneficial-ownership declaration; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; parent-bank SWIFT reference letter; board resolution appointing authorised signatories and confirming the absence of undisclosed nominees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aviation and food-supply counterparties domiciled in jurisdictions subject to sanctions or watchlists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed inflight-catering agreement with the operating airline including its IATA/ICAO codes; UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screening results for all counterparties, beneficial owners and aircraft operators; written export-control and sanctions compliance policy; list of airports and monthly uplift schedule proving physical intra-Egypt performance; covenant to notify the bank immediately of any change in the airline client base.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 41 / juridical person income tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the tax year; if the fiscal year ends 31 December, filing is due by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 2% per month on the unpaid tax; late filing administrative fine up to EGP 20,000; continued default may trigger tax attachment and strike-off of the corporate file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements filed with the companies registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Companies Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of financial year-end and before the annual ordinary general assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GAFI administrative fines generally from EGP 2,000 to EGP 50,000; official warning and possible suspension of the company file for continued non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the registration anniversary; changes in directors, members, or capital must be filed within 30 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late penalty starting at EGP 100 per month, delayed renewal may block issuance of official extract certificates and lead to administrative delistment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO / beneficial ownership confirmation declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI / Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) under Anti-Money Laundering Law 80/2002
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of the following year; each shareholding transfer must be reported within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EGP 100,000 for non-compliance under AML Law; refusal to record share transfer may follow from missing UBO updates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of airport inflight catering operational license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority (ECAA) / Relevant Governorate Licensing Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least 30 days before the annual license expiry date; the license term is determined by the issuing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of aircraft catering operations at Egyptian airports; administrative fines of EGP 10,000–100,000 and possible license revocation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs, regardless of revenue or asset size, must appoint one licensed external auditor and prepare audited annual financial statements. The audit is also statutorily required as a condition for GAFI annual registration confirmation and tax declaration submission.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially aligned with IFRS as endorsed by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority; IFRS is permissible for group consolidated filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation required each calendar year. The LLC must confirm all persons with ultimate ownership or control through shareholding chains and file an updated UBO disclosure with GAFI by 31 March. Every transfer of company shares must be reflected in the statutory register and reported to the Commercial Registry within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Meetings
Register of Charges or Encumbrances (where company assets are subject to security interests)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 1,500 typical annual registered-office or corporate-agent fee in Cairo / Alexandria
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 12,000 for an inflight catering LLC depending on revenue, number of transactions, and compliance complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory CIT holiday is generally available to an airport inflight catering LLC. Certain investment incentives under Investment Law 72/2017 may apply, principally a 30% deduction from taxable income for eligible capital investment, subject to GOEIC approval and sector criteria; airline catering is not automatically eligible. Suez Canal Economic Zone incentives, if the catering kitchen were registered within an authorized zone, could provide a reduced rate or additional deduction, but this is not assumed for the standard EG_LLC classification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return - Form No. 19 (Bayān 19), filed electronically through the Egypt Tax Authority e-filing portal (www.eta.gov.eg)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, no later than 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Commercial Registration and Tax Card Data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, commercial registry number, Tax Card number, Ministry of Supply catering license number, and head office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident LLCs operating through an Egyptian catering PE must quote its Egyptian Tax Card number and appoint a resident tax representative with notarized powers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: End date of the accounting period, usually 31 December, and the corresponding opening date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian PE must maintain books for the same fiscal year; depreciation schedules and advance payments must align with the ETA accounting calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from airline inflight meal production, ramp delivery, galley equipment handling, bonded storage fees, and aviation catering contracts invoiced in Egypt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-source revenue. If meals are sold through a foreign sister company while the Egyptian kitchen performs all production and ramp logistics, the PE-attributable share must be declared and transfer pricing documentation attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4a / Cost of Sales and Bonded Kitchen Expenditure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Food raw materials, kitchen labor, aircraft pre-boarding refrigeration, hygiene laboratory testing, quarantine inspection fees, packaging, and Cairo or airport storage costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident head-office costs are deductible only when the Egyptian PE books contain complete agreements, inbound customs records, and real business-purpose documentation for each cost allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent, payroll, social insurance and SAFE tax contributions, utilities, kitchen equipment leases, ETA withholding summaries, and amortization of catering facility improvements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Regional head-office overhead allocations require activity-based costing records and a TP policy; otherwise the ETA may apply a net-margin or deemed-profit assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Taxable Profit Before Loss Offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less allowable deductions and depreciation under Law No. 91 of 2005, adjusted for non-deductible expenditures, fines, and unsupported provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Translate all foreign-currency receipts into EGP at the Central Bank of Egypt rate on the invoice date; state whether the DTA Article 7 business-profits rule allocates profit solely to the Egyptian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unrelieved Egyptian tax losses from prior years, usable only within the five-year statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses economically attributable to the Egyptian PE may be deducted; losses suffered by a foreign legal entity cannot be transferred into the Egyptian PE return without explicit DTA and domestic analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit distributions or deemed profit distributions, the gross distributable amount, and the 10% dividend withholding tax remitted to the ETA on behalf of shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If dividends are declared to the foreign airline parent, enter the parent identity, shareholding percentage, and DTA article invoked; the statutory rate is 10% unless a prior ETA ruling confirms a treaty-reduced rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form No. 19 subjects the taxpayer to an incremental tax penalty of up to 25% of assessed tax and monthly interest of up to 2% on the unpaid amount. Fraudulent omission or false declaration may lead to penalties ranging from 100% to 200% of evaded tax, plus criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly CIT Advance Estimate and Payment Voucher, filed through the Egypt Tax Authority e-tax portal and payable at ETA-registered bank branches
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the end of the month following each tax quarter: 30 April, 31 July, 31 October, and 31 January for a calendar-year taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Projected taxable profit for the current fiscal year, using prior-year audited results adjusted for known catering contract volume changes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The estimate must be supported by signed airline meal purchase orders and foreign-currency hedging assumptions; a zero payment for a non-resident PE must be legally justified and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total advance corporate income tax already deposited with the ETA in the current fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach bank deposit vouchers; foreign taxes paid abroad cannot be credited unless a specific DTA credit article permits offset against Egyptian PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The amount due for the current quarter, computed either as one-fourth of the previous year's CIT liability or under an ETA-approved deemed-profit formula for newly registered taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The installment is provisional but becomes final assessment input; systematic underpayment triggers automatic penalties and ETA desk audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment by more than 20% of the correct quarterly installment results in a surcharge equal to 25% of the shortfall plus monthly interest of 2%. Repeated quarterly underreporting is treated as a red flag for expanded transfer pricing audit.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% dividend withholding tax on profit distributions by Egyptian LLCs and joint stock companies; a reduced 5% rate applies to distributions by companies listed on the Egyptian Exchange subject to listing and holding-period conditions. Non-resident airline parent companies may invoke a DTA to lower or eliminate the rate, typically to 5% or 0% under an eligible substantial-holding article.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) submit a written application to the Egypt Tax Authority before dividend distribution; (2) present a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the dividend recipient's jurisdiction, apostilled or consular legalized; (3) declare Beneficial Ownership in the distribution; (4) provide a factual memorandum showing compliance with the DTA's limitation-on-benefits or beneficial-ownership clause; and (5) obtain an ETA advance ruling confirming the reduced withholding rate. If tax has already been withheld at the statutory rate, a refund application may be filed within the five-year prescription period, supported by TRC, distribution minutes, and proof of remittance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents, kitchen software, menu formulations, or inflight catering trademarks paid to non-residents are subject to a 20% statutory Egyptian withholding tax. Interest on imported debt financing or supplier credit is subject to a 10% statutory withholding tax. DTA rates generally reduce royalties to 5%-15% and interest to 5%-10% among Egypt's treaty partners; treaty reductions are conditional upon Beneficial Ownership, absence of a permanent establishment in Egypt, and compliance with ETA relief order procedures.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are required for taxpayers whose total annual gross revenues exceed EGP 20 million and whose controlled related-party transaction values exceed EGP 10 million. The Transfer Pricing Disclosure return must accompany the annual Form No. 19 whenever the related-party transaction exceeds the regulatory threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a separate GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. However, the ETA applies the PE definition aligned with OECD and UN treaty practice, supported by General Anti-Avoidance Rules under Law 91/2005. An airline catering company claiming treaty benefits must show real decision-making, operational staff, physical kitchen and refrigeration presence, dispatch records, and a local board or management authority; otherwise the ETA may recharacterize or deny PE and treaty protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoicing of airline inflight catering revenue by routing meal contracts through a foreign sister company while the Egyptian kitchen performs all production, packaging, quarantine clearance, and ramp delivery at Cairo International Airport; or issuing fictitious import invoices for bonded raw materials without actual movement of goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessments on deemed profit of 15%-20% of gross catering turnover where books are rejected; incremental tax penalty of 25% of the evaded tax, monthly interest of 2%, fines of 100%-200% of tax evaded under Law No. 91 of 2005, and referral to the Economic Prosecution for criminal tax evasion. Imprisonment may range from two to five years, with publication of the conviction and revocation of the catering license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false returns or approved fake invoices are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and penalties. Civil restitution is supported by attachment of personal assets, bank accounts, and aviation contracts; travel bans may be ordered by the execution court, and a criminal conviction disqualifies directors from managing food supply or airline-related companies for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an EG_LLC as a letterbox entity with no real catering kitchen, no food-safety staff, no actual meal production, and no operational control, while a foreign parent airline directs all invoicing through the shell to avoid Egyptian CIT, customs duties, and employee taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may disregard the shell, reattribute all Egypt-source inflight catering income to a permanent establishment of the foreign parent, apply a deemed-profit assessment on gross catering service fees, disallow all management and royalty deductions, and impose estate-of-debt sanctions including fines and double penalties for abusive tax avoidance. The company's operating license may be revoked by the Civil Aviation and catering licensing authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who formed or maintained a sham entity face veil-piercing judgments for all unpaid Egyptian corporate tax, social insurance, and VAT-type obligations. Courts may impose civil restitution, personal travel bans, seizure of directors' residential properties, and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment of up to five years for misuse of corporate legal personality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and submit Local File, Master File, and the Transfer Pricing Disclosure return despite exceeding EGP 20 million annual gross revenue, coupled with non-arm's-length pricing on related-party transactions for frozen food, aviation crates, galley loading services, technical management fees, and equipment leases between the Egyptian catering LLC and the non-resident airline shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA makes adjustments using TNMM or Profit Split based on Egyptian food-service benchmark comparables, assesses arm's-length interest on the deficiency, levies an understatement penalty of up to 25%-50% of additional tax, and applies monthly 2% interest. The failure to provide TP documentation also blocks evidentiary rebuttal and triggers a higher-margin deemed assessment without entitlement to deduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where a director or tax supervisor deliberately refuses TP documentation requests, the personal liability regime applies to the resulting additional tax and penalties in proportion to fault. Courts may order the recovery of underpaid profits from directors' bank accounts, impose travel bans during tax subpoena proceedings, and prohibit the director from serving on any Egyptian tax-compliant board for a regulatory period.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in hawala settlements with airport concessionaires, failing to file cash transaction reports with the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit, making undocumented salary payments to catering workers, or using dual-use invoices to conceal countertrade of aviation food supplies across bonded customs zones.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended, sanctions include fines of up to EGP 200 million for entities, imprisonment of senior managers for three to seven years, freezing of bank accounts, confiscation of funds equal to the laundered amount, and cancellation of the customs bonded-airport license held by the catering operator.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Every director, compliance officer, and general manager who knowingly or negligently allowed hawala, ghost payroll, or unreported cash circulation is personally liable for fines and restitution. The criminal court may issue international arrest warrants, impose domestic travel bans, order asset seizure, and disqualify the individual from holding future catering licenses or duty-authority privileges in Egyptian airport zones.
